overview: Public sector and smart city systems decide on people's entitlements, services and shared infrastructure, so every decision must be lawful, explainable and open to appeal. Data is spread across agencies, equity matters as much as efficiency, and caseworkers and officials remain accountable for decisions about individuals.

concepts.name: Decisions about people need a legal basis and an appeal
concepts.explanation: Benefits, permits, tax and enforcement decisions follow statute and policy, and citizens can challenge them. Automated systems support officials and cannot replace the reasoning a decision must record.
concepts.whyItMatters: A model that cannot give reasons that match the law cannot be used for the final decision.

concepts.name: Equity and fairness are measured across groups
concepts.explanation: Services affect different neighbourhoods, languages and groups differently, and historical data can embed past exclusion. Public bodies often have a legal equality duty.
concepts.whyItMatters: Average accuracy hides differences, so outcomes should be checked across groups and areas.

concepts.name: Citizen service is multi-channel and multilingual
concepts.explanation: People contact government by phone, web, counter and post, in many languages, often at stressful moments. Good service gives consistent answers and a path to a human.
concepts.whyItMatters: An assistant that gives wrong guidance on entitlements can cost someone their benefit.

concepts.name: Cities run on shared infrastructure data
concepts.explanation: Traffic, transit, lighting, waste, water and buildings produce sensor and operational data owned by different departments. Value comes from joining them for operations and planning.
concepts.whyItMatters: Without shared identifiers and governance, every project builds its own isolated pipeline.

concepts.name: Planning relies on forecasts with uncertainty
concepts.explanation: Housing, schools, transport and services are planned from population, demand and land-use forecasts that carry wide uncertainty, so scenarios matter more than single numbers.
concepts.whyItMatters: A single forecast presented as certain can lock in the wrong capacity.

concepts.name: Fraud and error are different problems
concepts.explanation: Improper payments arise from fraud, administrative error and misunderstanding. Treating all of them as fraud leads to harmful accusations and chases the wrong cause.
concepts.whyItMatters: Cases flagged by a model should be reviewed by a person and handled proportionately.

concepts.name: Procurement and records are accountable by law
concepts.explanation: Public bodies must follow procurement rules, keep records and respond to freedom of information requests. AI systems need documented purpose, data sources and decision logs.
concepts.whyItMatters: A system that cannot be audited or explained to a regulator or journalist is a liability.

concepts.name: Data sharing between agencies is restricted
concepts.explanation: Agencies may share data only where law permits and for stated purposes. Linking records to build a profile of a person can breach purpose limits.
concepts.whyItMatters: Linking data for a new purpose needs legal review before any model is built.
